note: Page type hierarchy, v10. Three principles settled here. (1) A diagnostic procedure that produces a report is a RESULT: colonoscopy, catheterisation, endoscopy and laryngoscopy sit under Lab Report/Result > Diagnostic Study, not under Operative Note. Operative Note is for the operation itself. (2) A level that only names a service line is not a level: Cardiac Diagnostic and Neurodiagnostic are gone as L2s, folded into Diagnostic Study with the specialty carrying the service line. (3) No two L2 labels under one L1 may mean the same thing, so near-synonyms are merged rather than listed side by side. 'Others' sorts last at every level.

progress_note._comment: Progress Note is the only L1 whose L2 is decided by page CONTENT rather than by the document's family. It is resolved by the section tagger (sections/sections.json), not by family_map. L3 is blank: the client asked for the bigger sections only. L3_fine below is the finer split, kept so it is one flag away if it is ever wanted. 'Procedure' here is an in-office procedure described inside a note, which is a different thing from a formal operative report; those are L1 Operative Note.
progress_note._comment_dominance: When a page carries more than one section, the page takes the first of these that is present. Diagnosis and complaint outrank the data tables below them, because a page that states the visit diagnosis is about the visit even if two thirds of it is a lab grid.
progress_note._comment_sections: sections.json key -> coarse L2. Keys not listed here contribute no L2 (administrative is page furniture).
progress_note._comment_signature: A signature-only page: the closing page of a note carrying the attestation and little else. It is the End-of-document signal the boundary tagger already looks for, so it gets its own L2 rather than falling into Others.
progress_note._comment_merges: Plan of Care folds into Assessment and Plan, and History into CC/HPI, on client direction. Both pairs were splitting the same page in practice: a care plan IS the plan section, and past medical, social and family history are the background half of the present-illness narrative.

section_rank._comment: Dominance is ranked per SECTION, not per L2. Without this, folding History into CC/HPI silently promoted it: a page carrying a past medical history and a medication list used to resolve to Medication List, and would now resolve to CC/HPI purely because CC/HPI ranks second. The background-history sections keep the rank History had, so they win only when nothing else fired.

context_rules._comment: Rules that need the document the page sits in, so they run after the continuity step, not before it. A form or questionnaire bound into a progress note is part of that note; the same form standing alone as its own document is not.

page_types: Activities of Daily Living Flow Sheet
absorb_into_progress_note.comment: Standalone, these keep their Misc path (Screening and Checklist / Assessment and Evaluation).
absorb_into_progress_note._comment_split: A questionnaire page becomes L2 Questionnaire; a care plan page becomes L2 Plan of Care. Standing alone both keep their Misc path.
absorb_into_progress_note._comment_standalone: Standing alone these keep their own L1: Forms and Questionnaires for a questionnaire or care plan.

procedure_in_operative_document._comment: A procedure page bound into an operative document belongs to that operation: the intraoperative record, the phase record, the OR summary. The same page standing on its own is a treatment record and belongs to the Procedure Note L1. Deciding this by NAME is impossible, because both are called a procedure note, so it is decided by the document the page sits in. Runs after the continuity step, like the other context rules.

discharge_diagnosis_page.comment: A page whose dominant header is a diagnosis list, sitting inside a discharge packet, is the discharge diagnosis page. The same page standing alone in an outpatient note is Progress Note > Visit Diagnosis. L1 is decided by the document family first, so this only fires inside a discharge document. It only overrides the Depart/Discharge Note catch-all: a Transfer of Care or Interim Summary page keeps its own L2 even when its dominant section is a diagnosis list, because that page's identity is the handover, not the diagnosis.

notice_inside_consent_packet.comment: A notice about a policy is a consent wherever it sits, in a packet or on its own. Patient Communication > Notice keeps only notices that are not about a policy: a closure, a recall, a service change, a results-ready message.

collapse_L3._comment: L2 buckets that never expand to L3; L3 stays blank. Only the buckets with real page volume on the 624-page labelled set keep an L3 leaf, so this list is data, not logic in code.

L3_additions._comment: L3 leaves the client named that the canon did not carry as their own page type. CT angiography is a separate study from a plain CT: different protocol, different report, different code.

family_map._comment: page_family -> L1 and, outside Progress Note, L2. Progress Note families carry no L2 here: their L2 comes from the section tagger. 'specialty' is set only where the family was really a service line, and the document then takes a generic path.

page_type_overrides._comment: Page types that move somewhere other than their family's default. Under v5 the long list of specialty-note overrides collapses: every one of them is Progress Note with a specialty, and the L2 comes from the page content, so only the specialty needs stating.

Consent Form._comment: Was 'Others' before the signer rule of 2026-10-23 gave the generic forms a home.

Policy Page._comment: Any practice policy, privacy or patient-rights page is a consent, whether or not a signature line survived the scan: these pages exist to be acknowledged, and an unsigned copy is the same document waiting for a signature. Never Administrative. The two exceptions exist because the annotation tool's 'Policy Page' was also used for chart index pages and for insurance verification printouts, which are not policies at all.

Nursing Visit Note._comment: The home health nursing visit note (Briggs 3489 and its equivalents). A note is a Progress Note whatever service produced it; Home Health is the specialty, and 'homebound reason' is its tell.

_comment_specialty: Others = the page names a service line that is not one of the listed values. Unknown = no specialty signal on the page at all. They are different outcomes and the annotation tool must keep them apart: Others is a gap in this list, Unknown is a gap in the page.

L2_from_page_type._comment: L1s that were promoted out of Misc. Their subtree moved up a level, so the page type IS the L2 and L3 stays blank. Without this they would collapse to a single 'Others' L2.

flat_L1._comment: L1s with no L2 at all. The page type is the whole answer.

L2_merge._comment: Near-synonymous page types collapsed onto one L2 label, so no two L2s under an L1 can mean the same thing. An annotator who cannot tell two labels apart will use them interchangeably, and the model then learns a coin flip.

L3_merge._comment: L3 labels under one L2 that a reader cannot tell apart. Each pair below is one study under two names, or a subset silently competing with its own parent. Keeping both guarantees the annotators split on it and the model learns noise.

generic_leaf_rule._comment: A page type whose name is just its own parent's name is the generic case, not a sibling of the specific ones. 'Endoscopy Report' next to Colonoscopy, Cystoscopy and Bronchoscopy, or 'Consent Form' next to Surgical and Transfusion Consent Form, is a label an annotator reaches for when unsure, which is what 'Others' is for. Structural, so it needs no list: if the label's meaningful words are a subset of the parent's, the leaf is blanked and the parent stands alone.

lone_others_rule._comment: If 'Others' is the ONLY L2 under an L1 (or the only L3 under an L2) it carries no information: there is nothing for it to be other than. The level is dropped and the parent stands alone. Computed from the enumerated tree, so it stays correct as families are added.

implied_specialty_rule._comment: An implied specialty may only sit on a fully specified path. A row with a blank L3, or any row whose L2 or L3 is Others, is a BUCKET: Diagnostic Study holds cardiology, sleep, GI and ophthalmology studies alike, and Others holds whatever did not fit, so inheriting one member's specialty and printing it against the whole bucket is wrong. Taxonomy table only. At inference a page resolving into a bucket still gets its specialty from the detector reading the page, which is the right source for it.

_comment_page_artefact: Fax covers, blank pages, index and separator pages are removed by the junk filter before classification, so they carry no page type here. The canon keeps its Page Artefact entries so the filter has something to match on.

l2_catch_all_rule._comment: Where an L2 has named L3 children, its catch-all child is 'Others', not a blank. A blank L3 next to named siblings reads as missing data; Others reads as a decision. Where an L2 has no L3 children at all the L3 stays blank, because there is nothing to be other than.

no_L2_others._comment: L1s whose L2 set is closed: every page lands in one of the named buckets.

_comment_procedure_note: Procedure Note is a treatment RECORD: a repeated therapeutic session or an administration, which is neither an operation (Operative Note) nor an encounter narrative (Progress Note). Dialysis is the clearest case: a run is a procedure performed on a schedule, logged on a flow sheet, not a visit written up. Infusion, chemotherapy, radiation, wound care and the therapy disciplines behave the same way. The specialty still rides on the parallel axis, so Dialysis, Oncology, Wound Care and Rehabilitation are not lost by moving the document here.
_comment_procedure_L3: Procedure Note has no L3: the specific procedure IS the L2. A knee injection and a lumbar epidural are different procedures and different codes, so they sit at the same level as a dialysis run rather than one tier below it.
_comment_procedure_scope: Only procedures observed in the client's own page-type list or production volumes are carried. Site and modality variants that were not observed are deliberately absent: an empty class cannot be learned by the model and lengthens the annotator's dropdown for nothing. Add one when a page for it actually appears.
_comment_specialty_sweep: A page type implies a specialty only when the study itself names a service line. A mammogram is breast imaging and belongs to oncology; a CT is a CT and could be ordered by anyone. The deliberately unassigned ones are listed below so the decision is visible rather than looking like an omission: on those pages the specialty comes from the letterhead via the detector, or from the document by inheritance, or it is Unknown.

specialty_deliberately_unset.CT Scan Report: a CT can be ordered by any service; the body region is not in the page type
specialty_deliberately_unset.MRI Report: same as CT: the modality does not name a service line
specialty_deliberately_unset.Ultrasound Report: ordered by obstetrics, vascular, abdominal and musculoskeletal alike
specialty_deliberately_unset.X-Ray Report: the most service-neutral study there is
specialty_deliberately_unset.CT Angiography Report: cardiac, neuro and peripheral CTA are all common; the region is not in the name
specialty_deliberately_unset.Hematology Report: routine lab; haematology-oncology would be named in the letterhead, not the test
specialty_deliberately_unset.Urinalysis Report: routine lab; ordered far more often by primary care than urology
specialty_deliberately_unset.INR and Prothrombin Time: routine coagulation monitoring, no service line
specialty_deliberately_unset.Laboratory Flow Sheet: a trended grid of whatever was ordered

mece_rules._comment: Three L1s can all receive something a human would call a form. The discriminator is what the form DOES, not that it is a form. Applied in this order, the three are mutually exclusive and between them exhaustive.

form_routing.test: grants a permission and carries a patient or guardian signature
captures identity, contact or coverage, with no clinical content
collects clinical information about the patient, scored or free text
a billing or scheduling page: a statement, invoice, superbill, appointment list or no-show letter
a practice policy, rights or responsibilities page the patient signs or acknowledges
examples: Notice of Privacy Practices with signature line

form_routing.test: an insurance or benefit verification page the practice or payer produced
a chart artefact with no clinical or financial content: a document index, an import log, a fax banner page

consent_vs_authorization._comment: Replaced 2026-10-23. The old test asked what the page permitted, which split badly: a HIPAA release permits a disclosure and is signed by the patient, so it answered both ways. The test is now who issues it.
consent_vs_authorization.test: who signs or issues the page
consent_vs_authorization.consent: the patient or their guardian signs it, including acknowledging a notice
consent_vs_authorization.authorization: the hospital, provider or payer issues it
consent_vs_authorization.when_no_signature_block_is_legible: fall back to the title: a page titled consent is a consent, a page titled authorization issued on practice or payer letterhead is an authorization, otherwise General Consent if addressed to the patient and Others if neither

hipaa_pages._comment: Both sides of a HIPAA page are patient-signed, so both are consents. The split is only how specific it is.
hipaa_pages.names_a_recipient: Consent and Authorization > Release of Information
hipaa_pages.acknowledges_the_notice_only: Consent and Authorization > HIPAA and Privacy

context_resolved_pairs._comment: Three L2 labels exist under more than one L1. They are not duplicates: the PATH differs, and which one applies is decided by the document the page is bound into, not by the page. All three run after the continuity step. Listed here so the collision reads as a designed pair rather than an oversight, and so the annotation tool can show both options with the rule.

pairs.label: Medication List
pairs.rule: a medication table printed inside a note is part of that note

pairs.label: Questionnaire
pairs.rule: a form bound into a note is part of that note; this one also flips codeability

pairs.label: Procedure
pairs.rule: a procedure page in an operative document belongs to that operation

referral_pages._comment: Three different pages are all called referrals. They are separated by who wrote them and what the page does, which is the same signer test used for consent and authorization.
referral_pages.tell_them_apart: a referral order names the specialty or provider being referred TO and carries the referring provider's signature; a referral authorization carries an approval or reference number, a validity period and payer letterhead

_comment_podiatry: Foot and ankle care. Named Podiatry rather than 'Foot and Ankle' because the letterhead evidence is the DPM credential and the word podiatry; 'foot and ankle' is carried as an alias. It overlaps Orthopedics by body site, so the rule is the provider, not the anatomy: a DPM or a podiatry practice is Podiatry, an orthopedic surgeon operating on a foot is Orthopedics. Rename to 'Foot and Ankle' in this list and in specialty.json if the client prefers that wording.

consent_auth_side._comment: Who issues the page decides which word applies. The patient gives consent; the hospital, provider or payer gives authorization. This is a test about the signer, not about the word printed in the title: a page headed 'Authorization for Release of Information' is signed by the patient and is therefore a consent.
consent_auth_side._comment_reassigned: Two L2s moved to the consent side under this rule despite carrying the word authorization in their usual titles. Release of Information is signed by the patient permitting a disclosure. Assignment of Benefits is signed by the patient assigning payment. Both are patient-given, so both are consents. Flagged because the naming reads the other way.
consent_auth_side._comment_notice: A notice page is a consent when it sits in a consent packet or carries a patient signature or acknowledgement line. A notice the practice merely sends out, with nothing for the patient to sign, stays Patient Communication > Notice.

_comment_administrative_scope: Administrative means money or scheduling, nothing else. Billing statements, invoices, superbills, statements of account, payment plans; appointment lists, no-show letters, scheduling notes. The old 'Administrative Record' catch-all was removed on 2026-10-23 because it had become a home for anything non-clinical: 15 of its 19 pages were financial-policy and patient-rights pages the patient signs, which are consents, and insurance verification pages, which are authorizations. A catch-all under a vague L1 attracts exactly the pages that belong somewhere specific.
